stem: A thriving breastfed infant with loose stools has a fresh stool sample tested and reducing substances are 0.4%; what is the best interpretation?

options.text: This can be a normal finding in a breastfed infant
This confirms clinically significant carbohydrate malabsorption
This result is impossible if the sample is fresh
This means osmotic diarrhoea has been excluded

explanation: Normal stool reducing substances. In a thriving breastfed infant, up to 0.5% reducing substances can be a normal finding, so 0.4% does not by itself indicate disease.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because in a breastfed infant, reducing substances of 0.4% can fall within the normal range and must be interpreted in clinical context.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this level alone does not confirm clinically significant carbohydrate malabsorption.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a fresh sample can still show reducing substances, and this value may be normal in a breastfed infant.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because this result does not specifically diagnose sucrose malabsorption.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a normal or near-normal reducing substances result does not exclude osmotic diarrhoea or other causes of loose stools.
